CweFindings.Name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.uploadPhotos lines 57-68 only rejects null/empty multipart lists, then iterates every supplied file with database/upload work at lines 69-89. The advertised app.file-upload.max-files-per-upload setting at application.properties:30 is never bound or checked. An authenticated caller can submit many small parts, causing work proportional to caller-controlled file count rather than the configured ten-file bound. The 50MB request limit constrains total bytes, and servlet multipart limits may further constrain part count; no infinite loop or unbounded single-request byte size is claimed.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Initialization
CweFindings.Description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.
CweFindings.Explanation: application.properties:19 and application-docker.properties:15 configure Hibernate ddl-auto=create against the application database, while docker-compose.yml:31 selects the docker profile and lines 12-13 persist database state. Hibernate create initialization drops/recreates mapped schema objects on application startup, discarding existing photo rows despite persistent database storage. This is a startup data-integrity/initialization risk in the shipped configuration, not an attacker-triggered remote exploit; an intentional disposable development deployment would narrow its impact.

CweFindings.Name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
CweFindings.Description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.
CweFindings.Explanation: Public HomeController.index lines 37-41 calls getAllPhotos, whose PhotoRepository.findAllOrderByUploadedAtDesc query at lines 22-27 selects PHOTO_DATA for every row without pagination or a result bound. Photo.photoData lines 39-41 is a byte[] LOB with default eager fetching, so the entire stored image corpus is materialized in memory even though the page only needs metadata. Dataset size is influenced by authenticated uploads; any anonymous gallery request can then trigger a size-proportional allocation that may exhaust the 512MB container heap (Dockerfile:28). The per-file/request caps and image pixel guard do not bound aggregate gallery allocation. No load test or exact exhaustion threshold was measured.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: SecurityConfig.securityFilterChain lines 46-61 enables HTTP Basic authentication but configures no authentication/security-event audit handler or listener. Production code has no audit event consumer. PhotoServiceImpl.uploadPhoto lines 179-180 and deletePhoto line 212 log security-critical data mutations with photo identifiers/filenames but omit the authenticated principal and request origin/correlation; DetailController.deletePhoto line 69 likewise omits actor identity. Consequently the application does not provide attributable audit records for mutations, and application-level recording of failed authentication is not configured. This is a logging/traceability gap, not evidence that authentication is bypassed. External gateway or separately configured runtime audit logs were not available to verify.

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoServiceImpl.uploadPhoto lines 87-94 trusts the multipart Content-Type; lines 130-158 do not reject files without an image reader or with dimension-parsing failures, and lines 160-174 persist the original bytes. Thus an authenticated uploader can store non-image or dangerous-type bytes by declaring an allowed image MIME type; bytes are examined by ImageIO and subsequently served unchanged by PhotoFileController.servePhoto lines 74-83. No server-side execution or browser script execution is established; image MIME responses and framework nosniff headers limit those consequences.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: upload.js showErrors lines 215-218 interpolates untrusted filenames into innerHTML. handleFiles lines 71-82 includes local file.name in errors; uploadFiles lines 118-120 includes server-returned failedUploads.fileName from HomeController.uploadPhotos lines 86-89. A markup-bearing filename can introduce active HTML into the uploading browser. createPhotoCard lines 181-190 also inserts originalFileName without escaping via insertAdjacentHTML line 157. Server-rendered Thymeleaf text is escaped, so cross-user persistent exploitation through the normal gallery is not established; authenticated success uploads and victim interaction/file selection constrain reachability.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
CweFindings.Description: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream component. Without sufficient removal or quoting of SQL syntax in user-controllable inputs, the generated SQL query can cause those inputs to be interpreted as SQL instead of ordinary user data.
CweFindings.Explanation: create-user.sh lines 19, 22-30 expands environment-supplied schema identity and password directly into SQLPlus heredoc SQL, including the single-quoted username predicate at line 27 and nested EXECUTE IMMEDIATE statement at line 30, without escaping SQL literal/identifier delimiters. An operator-supplied value containing SQL delimiters can alter privileged initialization SQL. This is a deployment/configuration-input injection pattern, not a remotely reachable HTTP SQL injection; it requires influence over initialization environment variables. Production PhotoRepository queries use bound parameters and do not demonstrate SQL injection.
